content: MS searches for partitions at each Markov time that maximise $r(t,H)$ . Although the maximisation of ( 5 ) is an NP-hard problem (hence with no guarantees for global optimality), there are efficient optimisation methods that work well in practice. Our implementation here uses the Louvain Algorithm BIBREF35 , BIBREF12 which is efficient and known to give good results when applied to benchmarks BIBREF36 . To obtain robust partitions, we run the Louvain algorithm 500 times with different initialisations at each Markov time and pick the best 50 with the highest Markov Stability value $r(t,H)$ . We then compute the variation of information BIBREF37 of this ensemble of solutions $VI(t)$ . as a measure of the reproducibility of the result under the optimisation. In addition, the relevant partitions are required to be persistent across time, as given by low values of the variation of information between optimised partitions across time $VI(t,t^{\prime })$ . Robust partitions are thus indicated by Markov times where $VI(t)$ shows a dip and $VI(t,t^{\prime })$ has an extended plateau, indicating consistent results from different Louvain runs and validity over extended scales BIBREF34 , BIBREF10 .
